definitions.gloss: to button up wrong; to fasten buttons in the wrong holes
definitions.explanation: To put buttons through the wrong buttonholes, causing the garment to be misaligned.

definitions.gloss: to have a fundamental misunderstanding; to go wrong from the start
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively to describe a situation where communication or a relationship has gone off track due to an initial misunderstanding, like buttons fastened in the wrong holes.

examples.japanese: ⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}えて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Your buttons are done up wrong.

examples.japanese: ⟦シャツ→シャツ：01052_shatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}えたまま⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}って→行く：00119_iku⟧しまった。
examples.english: I went to work with my shirt buttoned up wrong.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧、⟦{急|いそ}いでいて→急ぐ：01191_isogu⟧⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}えた。
examples.english: I was in a rush this morning and buttoned my shirt wrong.

examples.japanese: ⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{壊|こわ}した→壊す：01241_kowasu⟧。
examples.english: A fundamental misunderstanding destroyed their relationship.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}える⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{全部|ぜんぶ}→全部：02888_zenbu⟧⟦ずれて→ずれる：03370_zureru⟧しまう。
examples.english: If you get the first button wrong, everything else is off — just like a misunderstanding from the start.

examples.japanese: ⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{初期|しょき}→初期：11742_shoki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}えたこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対立|たいりつ}→対立：04500_tairitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つながった。
examples.english: Getting things wrong at the start of negotiations led to later conflicts.

notes:
The literal meaning (sense 1) is straightforward. The figurative meaning (sense 2) is very common and uses the metaphor of misaligned buttons to describe how an initial small mistake or misunderstanding cascades into larger problems.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}える: to button wrongly (literal and figurative)
- ⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}い: a mis-buttoning; a fundamental misunderstanding (noun form)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{食|く}い{違|ちが}う→食い違う：16321_kuichigau⟧: to disagree, to be at odds — focuses on a discrepancy between two things
- ⟦{誤解|ごかい}→誤解：02769_gokai⟧: misunderstanding — more general, without the metaphorical nuance

CULTURAL NOTE:
The metaphor ⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{違|ちが}い is widely understood in Japanese and often appears in discussions about relationships, diplomacy, and communication breakdowns.
